questions.q: Phenol is warmed with NaNO₂ and concentrated H₂SO₄, the mixture is poured into water, and then NaOH is added. The sequence of colours is:
questions.explain: Remember 'GRB': deep green to blue in concentrated acid, red on dilution with water, and blue again in alkali. All three colours come from one dye, phenolindophenol, in different protonation states.

questions.q: Which phenol normally gives a NEGATIVE Liebermann nitroso test?
questions.explain: Nitrosation occurs at the para position, so a para-substituted phenol such as p-cresol usually gives no colour. Hydroquinone and 4-iodophenol are the stated exceptions that still react.

questions.q: The coloured compound formed in the Liebermann nitroso test is:
questions.explain: p-Nitrosophenol (as benzoquinone monoxime) is only the intermediate; it condenses with a second phenol molecule in concentrated acid to give the indophenol dye O=C₆H₄=N–C₆H₄–OH.

questions.q: An aliphatic amine gives a yellow oily liquid with NaNO₂ and dilute HCl in the cold, and this oil gives a positive Liebermann test with phenol and concentrated H₂SO₄. The amine is:
questions.explain: A secondary amine forms an N-nitrosamine (the yellow oil), which hands its nitroso group to phenol in hot acid. Primary aliphatic amines give N₂ gas instead, and tertiary aliphatic amines give no nitroso compound.
